title: Recovering a Boolean value from its code
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type, let $L$ be a natural number at least $|\alpha|$, and let $a\colon\alpha\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. Encode $a$ as a Boolean list of length $L$ by placing its values in the order given by an enumeration of $\alpha$ and padding with false values. Then the list entry at the position of any $i\in\alpha$ is exactly $a(i)$.
hypotheses_covered: $a$ assigns a Boolean value to each element of $\alpha$
